clue.text: Gadget for film or photography that's part of the machine age

parts.note: a cam is a rotating part of a machine that converts motion
an era is an age or period

explanation.surface: A camera is described as a typical gadget of the mechanical age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of the machine age' reads as one phrase but splits into the machine part and the age.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the device used to take photographs or shoot film.

clue.text: Forest dweller still in its youth's a horny spirit, we hear

definitions.text: Forest dweller still in its youth

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word for the spirit is taken by its sound

parts.note: a faun is a horned woodland spirit of Roman myth

explanation.surface: A young woodland creature is compared to a lustful sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horny' means horned here, not lustful.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawn is a deer in its first year, a young forest animal.

clue.text: CIA meeting with Boris for a change, levelly maintaining pressure

indicators.note: making a change to the letters signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: The CIA meets Boris for once, keeping things calm under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobaric describes conditions of equal or constant pressure, as on weather-map isobars.

clue.text: Fancy peccadillo finally committed away from home

indicators.note: to be committed is to be put into something, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: away from home means not in

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of peccadillo

explanation.surface: A minor sin, finally done while on a trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or a fancy is an idea or whim.

clue.text: A pair of experts tackling sort of dog that can be secured

indicators.note: the experts tackle, or take hold of, the dog, so it ends up between them

parts.note: a pro and someone able are two kinds of expert
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Two specialists take on a dog that can be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pair of experts' means two different words for an expert, which split apart to hold the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Procurable means obtainable, something that can be got hold of.

clue.text: One's learned to be vigilant about roaming charges

definitions.text: One's learned to be vigilant about roaming charges

parts.words: One's learned to be vigilant about roaming charges
parts.note: reads like a phone customer wary of overseas fees, but the charges are animals in one's care that wander

explanation.surface: A traveller has learned to watch out for mobile roaming fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' are the animals in its care and 'roaming' means wandering about, not phone use abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A working farm dog is trained to watch the flock and keep straying animals together.

clue.text: Initially mysterious pseudonyms shifting one's anxious feelings

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of mysterious
shifting tells us one letter of the word changes position

parts.note: aliases are false names, pseudonyms

explanation.surface: Changing strange pen names leaves someone feeling uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' moves the first I of ALIASES along to give ALAISES.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general sense of unease or discomfort.

clue.text: US representative drills through ecclesiastical site (it's a source of oil)

indicators.note: drilling through something puts one piece into the middle of another

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat or diocese
Uncle Sam personifies the United States

explanation.surface: An American official drills through a church site, bracketing it as an oil source.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds are pressed to yield a cooking oil.

clue.text: Influential American wants one of Groucho's kin sent into retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the brother's name is read backwards

parts.note: Harpo was one of Groucho Marx's brothers

explanation.surface: A powerful American wants a Marx brother pensioned off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marx Brothers were a US comedy team; Harpo was the silent one.
explanation.definitionFit: Oprah Winfrey is a hugely powerful US talk-show host and media figure.

clue.text: Church stands next to empty Russian laboratory

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: emptying the word leaves just its outside letters

explanation.surface: A church sits beside a deserted Russian research lab.
explanation.definitionFit: CERN is the European particle-physics research centre near Geneva.

clue.text: Unusual chemise and odd robe regularly stained

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
regularly takes every other letter, here the even ones of odd robe

explanation.surface: An odd chemise and a strange robe end up soiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like an adjective, but it is fodder: 'regularly' takes D, R, B from 'odd robe', and these join CHEMISE in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmirch is to dirty or sully, literally or a reputation.

clue.text: Someone in The Imitation Game, perhaps?

definitions.text: Someone in The Imitation Game, perhaps?

parts.words: Someone in The Imitation Game, perhaps?
parts.note: The Imitation Game is a film about Alan Turing, and anyone in a film is a performer; imitating is also what such a person does

explanation.surface: A question about who appears in the Turing film.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title doubles as a description of the profession: an imitation game is acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Film performers play parts, imitating other people for an audience.

clue.text: Performers of one kind or another taking lead from tempo instead of libido

indicators.note: taking one letter instead of another means a swap of letters
instead of marks the letter being replaced

parts.note: lap dancers are another kind of performer
the lead, or first letter, of libido is L, also shared via 'lead from'

indicators.note: the lead is the first letter of tempo and of libido

explanation.surface: Dancers swap a sultry motive for a sense of rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the L of lap dancers to T, the first letter of 'tempo' replacing that of 'libido'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dancers are entertainers who dance in metal-soled shoes.

clue.text: Made from denim, Rodin's first couple of pieces took subject less seriously

indicators.note: broken into pieces, the letters are put back together differently
the first couple of letters means the opening two

explanation.surface: A sculpture made from denim, Rodin's earliest works.
explanation.walkthrough: RO, the first two letters of 'Rodin's', joins DENIM to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A US student who minored in a subject studied it as a secondary course.

clue.text: Lines going around the world will snub Luther's latest theses

indicators.note: snubbing something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: the tropics are lines of latitude circling the globe

indicators.note: the latest letter is the final one

explanation.surface: The world will cold-shoulder Luther's newest theses.
explanation.walkthrough: Luther's 95 theses invite reading 'theses' with him; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward for discussion, a subject or topic.

clue.text: Cockney's extremely vigorous when holding up flight, ultimately making you the last to arrive

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower part holds up what sits above it
ultimately picks the final letter
a Cockney speaker drops the H sound

parts.note: hardiest means most robust or vigorous

explanation.surface: A Cockney is at his most vigorous delaying a flight, making him last in.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, traditional working-class Londoners, drop their Hs; 'holding up' in a down answer puts the last letter of 'flight' on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiest means latest of all, the one who arrives after everyone.

clue.text: Parasite essentially libels medic with virus

indicators.note: the essence of each word is its centre, so the middle letters are taken

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a virus

explanation.surface: A parasite basically slanders the doctor carrying the infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes BE from the middle of 'libels' and D from the middle of 'medic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedbugs are blood-sucking insects living off a host.

clue.text: Big reveal sees English banker trap unknown figure by safe

indicators.note: trapping something holds it inside

parts.note: a banker is a river, having banks; the Po is Italy's longest
x is the classic unknown in algebra
sure means safe, certain

explanation.surface: A big revelation shows an English banker trapping a mysterious figure near a safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword shorthand for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposure is a revealing of something hidden, such as a scandal.

clue.text: Certain philosophers revolutionised science with big apple

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: the Big Apple is New York City

explanation.surface: Science was transformed in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionised' reverses SCI plus NYC as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cynics were an ancient Greek school of philosophy founded by Antisthenes.

clue.text: Effortlessly quirky Dali bored by a certain piece in Spain? On the contrary

indicators.note: being bored by something puts that thing into you
this reverses the roles, so the artist goes inside instead

parts.note: rey is Spanish for king, a chess piece

indicators.note: quirky means odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The eccentric Dali is bored by a piece in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quirky' scrambles the painter's name; 'bored by' would put the Spanish king inside it, but 'On the contrary' flips that so the king surrounds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Readily means with ease, without difficulty.

clue.text: Writer had visor and mask lifted now and again to deliver some vernacularisms

parts.note: the writer refers to themself as I

indicators.note: letters lifted only now and again means every other one is taken

explanation.surface: A writer lifts visor and mask occasionally to talk plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted now and again' takes IOMS, alternate letters of 'visor' and 'mask' run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Idioms are expressions peculiar to a language's everyday speech.

clue.text: Urge some lesser Pentagon characters to turn to the other side

indicators.text: to turn to the other side
indicators.note: turning to the other side reverses the direction of reading
some of the letters of the words are taken, hidden in them

explanation.surface: Urge some lower Pentagon staff to defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds SSERP inside 'lesser Pentagon' and 'to turn to the other side' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge or push them.

clue.text: Post for Methuselah? (Letters for 26 others are enclosed here too)

definitions.text: Post for Methuselah? (Letters for 26 others are enclosed here too)

parts.words: Post for Methuselah? (Letters for 26 others are enclosed here too)
parts.note: Methuselah is this crossword's compiler, so his post or job is the compiler's; the bracket suggests mail with letters enclosed

explanation.surface: Mail for Methuselah, with letters for others enclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' is a job, not mail; Methuselah is the pseudonym of this puzzle's compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword compiler is called a setter in British usage.

clue.text: Desperately stir acidic bits of crème fraîche?

indicators.note: done desperately, the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A cook frantically stirs acidic bits of sour cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bits' are the accents on è and î, not lumps of cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Diacritics are accent marks such as the grave and circumflex in the phrase.

clue.text: Greek character placing ring on yours truly — much obliged!

indicators.note: placing the ring next to the first letter sets the order of the pieces
on means the ring comes after, attached to, the first letter

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, I
O is a ring shape
ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone thanks another for placing a ring on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Little monkeys and little apes scratching skin on crotch

indicators.note: scratching something out removes it

parts.note: chimps is the short form of chimpanzees

indicators.note: the skin is the outside, first and last letters

explanation.surface: Small apes scratch an itchy crotch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' in 'Little monkeys' means mischievous children.
explanation.definitionFit: Little monkeys and imps are both playful mischievous children.

clue.text: During chorus, trumpeters play strings

indicators.note: the answer runs within the words, during them

explanation.surface: In the chorus the brass play string instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum is to brush across the strings of a guitar.

clue.text: Soprano picked up yeti, perhaps, as a bit of theatrical action

definitions.text: as a bit of theatrical action

parts.note: S is the musical abbreviation for soprano

indicators.note: picking up means hearing, so the word goes by sound

parts.note: a cryptid is an animal like the yeti whose existence is unproven

explanation.surface: A soprano listened out for a yeti in a stage scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage action written into a play's text is scripted, planned rather than improvised.
